study.question: Can explicitly separating task-positive history content from task-positive history mass improve evolving field/task queries without rewriting history keys? Observed starting point: incumbent macro AUC 0.811178251 versus DIN 0.809923388, but macro Logloss 0.056800382 versus 0.056622951 and click AUC 0.654271684 versus 0.655544082. The current code uses a single validity mask for every query and only a total-length scalar; the provided per-task action masks are unused. Positive-history scarcity is an uncertainty, not an observed failure. Parent versus DIN task deltas: is_click: AUC 0.654271684 (delta -0.001272398), Logloss 0.183838932 (delta +0.000442129); cart: AUC 0.847840247 (delta -0.001229455), Logloss 0.019925337 (delta +0.000043156); fav: AUC 0.868588127 (delta +0.003690634), Logloss 0.015053921 (delta +0.000100581); buy: AUC 0.874012946 (delta +0.003830671), Logloss 0.008383338 (delta +0.000123856)
study.hypothesis: Provisional mechanism: an all-history softmax forces rare feedback events to compete with exposures, and pooled-value LayerNorm removes much of absolute evidence scale. A dedicated task-mask-normalized read can supply positive-action content while a separate count path supplies its quantity. Mixing these task messages with fields before the next query lets behavior semantics alter later field-conditioned retrieval while keeping history keys static. The 1:1 global/specific blend retains cross-behavior evidence. This explanation is not established by existing scores. Trajectory review: all original exchange arms underperformed DIN; the apparent helpful reverse-write effect in round 0 did not transfer to later value replacements. Wide values did not establish a preservation benefit, and the round-1 write/value interaction changed direction. In round 2, value-only/key-only/both writes all trailed the no-write control. Its 0.810733395 score also differs from the incumbent by -0.000444856, warning against treating tiny same-seed implementation differences as robust effects. No failed execution receipts are supplied and previous_runtime_error is null. Full supplied trajectory: baseline-din: AUC=0.809923388, Logloss=0.056622951, wall=329.1s; g1-r0000-exchange_full: AUC=0.804828231, Logloss=0.056985564, wall=809.1s; g1-r0000-exchange_read_only: AUC=0.796032245, Logloss=0.057379408, wall=805.6s; g1-r0000-exchange_fixed_query: AUC=0.804114955, Logloss=0.057133034, wall=803.9s; g1-r0000-exchange_fixed_both: AUC=0.797518256, Logloss=0.057234900, wall=803.5s; g1-r0001-wide_feedback: AUC=0.806539687, Logloss=0.056860680, wall=839.7s; g1-r0001-lowrank_feedback: AUC=0.806364298, Logloss=0.056742222, wall=833.9s; g1-r0001-wide_static: AUC=0.804769822, Logloss=0.056864902, wall=832.7s; g1-r0001-lowrank_static: AUC=0.811178251, Logloss=0.056800382, wall=839.6s; g1-r0002-value_feedback_only: AUC=0.809554624, Logloss=0.056697632, wall=865.0s; g1-r0002-key_feedback_only: AUC=0.807626647, Logloss=0.056910282, wall=854.3s; g1-r0002-feedback_both: AUC=0.805885987, Logloss=0.056741039, wall=858.7s; g1-r0002-feedback_neither: AUC=0.810733395, Logloss=0.056909381, wall=861.3s

Here evolving task queries repeatedly read matching historical-action subsets plus global history with shared projections, a separate log-count input and static event keys. No proxy broadcast backbone or original-method equivalence is claimed; novelty remains unverified.

We reuse the mask-derived grouping idea, not that architecture. Our task-mask restrictions remain active at each task retrieval and final value read, with explicit attention-denominator masking and a per-query zero null.

Pinned source lines 119-156 and 198-282 inspected. Repeated field/history retrieval is already inherited from local work; this study adds a matching-action task stream and a separately controlled count signal, without EST token-specific Q/O, heterogeneous FFNs, sequence FFNs or a claimed original-paper audit.

study.proposed_difference: R: concatenate four duplicate task queries to each shared read and use query-specific masks: all-history masks for original field/task queries and the corresponding positive-action mask for each added task query. Blend the two task reads 1:1 before each existing field/task mixer and similarly blend the final wide-value reads before the inherited low-rank reconstruction. K/V sequence projection is computed once per read; no event rewrite or sequence self-attention is added. C: append a shared bias-free Linear(1,32), constructed after inherited initialization, to map each task masked-positive log count into its initial task token. Every arm computes all masks, queries, reads and count projections. Global validity intersects every task mask; overlapping action groups stay overlapping. Per-query null keys are enabled only for empty groups, after normalization, with bias-free Q/K/V/output. Fixed inherited settings are dynamic_query=true, raw_values=false, event_feedback=false. Estimated registered capacity is parent +32 dense parameters = 32,115,044 total / 321,828 dense, subject to host confirmation. Local code is syntax/source checked only; PyTorch is unavailable. New performance and runtime are unknown.
predictions: Predeclared primary joint prediction: macro AUC(R1C1)>macro AUC(R0C0), and R1C1 exceeds the incumbent 0.8111782509544756 if it is to replace it. Selection still uses the existing macro-AUC rule and all declared tie breakers, without a newly invented effect threshold or per-task veto.

Routing mechanism prediction: positive routing deltas at fixed C=0 and C=1; count prediction: positive count deltas at fixed R=0 and R=1. Report main effects and A11-A10-A01+A00; a winning joint arm alone establishes neither constituent mechanism.

Exploratory slice prediction: gains should concentrate in nonempty histories, especially history_gt64 where incumbent click AUC 0.651291017 trails DIN 0.657803100. No improvement is predicted for empty-history evidence; empty_history has only 13 buy positives, 28 fav positives, 45 cart positives and 427 click positives, so its rare-task AUC is unstable.

All four arms have identical registered parameter count, seed and operation structure, but extra queries can increase actual runtime over the incumbent. Report wall/train/inference time, p50/p95 batch latency and peak memory; make an efficiency claim only from measured quality/cost comparisons.

Use only host-provided validation feedback. Report four task AUC and Logloss values and deltas against both baseline-din and g1-r0001-lowrank_static, plus macro Logloss, slice sample/positive/negative counts and unavailable diagnostics. No test data or closed assessment may be requested.
falsifiers: If R1C1 does not beat R0C0 on macro AUC, the joint implementation has no observed predictive support; if counts_only is as good or better, the joint information-flow explanation is not supported.

If both conditional routing effects are nonpositive, task-mask routing lacks support in this implementation even if counts help. If both conditional count effects are nonpositive, the explicit-count component lacks support even if routing helps. Conflicting effects require an interaction explanation and repetition.

Before interpreting training results, host checks must confirm initial R0C0 versus parent predictions and active gradients match within appropriate FP32/BF16 tolerance, with identical inherited initialization. Different SDPA query shapes can alter BF16 rounding. A material endpoint mismatch is implementation counterevidence to resolve, not a valid mechanism contrast.

Host preflight must test all-padding, zero-length and mixed histories, individual empty action groups, overlapping masks, padding-token perturbations, finite predictions/BCE/backward and all four [B,1] outputs. Changing masked padding or the unknown current-target action must not change predictions; a null-only action read must be zero even after learned LayerNorm biases. Any failure invalidates the associated contrast and remains charged.

A later paired-seed reversal leaves effects preliminary. A later count-preserving permuted-mask or readout-only match would weaken task-semantic or layer-wise coupling attribution. This initial factorial does not replace those follow-ups.
alternative_explanations: One frozen training seed and one data pass; sensitivity to BF16 rounding and optimizer dynamics remains. Repeating a seed is not a new mechanism contrast.

The R intervention bundles matching-mask selection, group normalization and a fixed 1:1 blend at two internal reads plus final pooling. It does not separately identify these three read sites or semantic alignment versus any mask-induced regularization.

Empty positive groups receive zero from their specific branch and half the global evidence when R=1; this can encode group absence even with C=0. Counts and routing are therefore not informationally independent.
Registered capacity is matched; the 32 count-map weights have zero effective gradient when C=0. This study cannot prove that equal registered parameters imply equal effective capacity.
No measured positive-history support distribution is supplied. Very sparse feedback groups could make hard within-group normalization noisy.
The released offline feedback visibility and user/category/brand auxiliary label semantics limit production interpretation.

Count gains may be a simple behavioral-frequency shortcut rather than evidence of joint representation evolution. Routing can help through variance reduction or normalization rather than task semantics.
Capacity or value-normalization changes explained some earlier trajectories, so the new study holds those paths fixed. Repeated scores across the same user exposures are not independent replications.

cost_plan.estimate_ref: Measured full units: baseline-din 329.1s, g1-r0001-lowrank_static 839.6s and round-2 controls/candidate 854.3-865.0s; not the stale 483.4s initial estimate. Expect roughly 900-1100s per new full unit from added task queries with shared K/V; this is unmeasured and can be wrong. Existing hard per-trial cap 1208.5413760878146s remains unchanged. Four trials at the cap total 4834.2s; allow at most a further 600s charged host preflight/diagnostics, not an extra training trial. Runtime reports 31616.4s remaining at context delivery; the host ledger/deadline is authoritative and all preparation/tool calls count.
cost_plan.attribution_reserve: Reserve 6000s for charged failure investigation, an optimized selected-path implementation only if warranted, and one discriminating mask-alignment or internal-versus-readout contrast plus its matched control. This is reserved future work, not extra variants silently authorized here. Do not use repeated initializations as a substitute for those contrasts.
cost_plan.assessment_reserve: Reserve 10000s for a frozen validation-only comparison suite and up to three paired seeds of the selected candidate, closest concurrent control and initial DIN reference, with checkpoint/source/config hashes and per-task/cost reporting. Use only the authorized host repetition interface if subsequently exposed; no seed override in model config. User-cluster bootstrap is conditional on the host exposing authorized paired validation predictions and cluster identities; raw IDs are not available to the model. Otherwise report it unavailable and keep conclusions preliminary. Held-out assessment is unavailable in this rerun.
cost_plan.stop_rule: Stop at the existing hard deadline/cap or user stop, on information-boundary or scoring-integrity failure, or when no useful admissible experiment plus attribution/assessment reserves fits the live remaining budget. Never increase a cap, change the frozen host recipe, install dependencies, train in this coding jail, retry unknown-state host jobs automatically or treat exhausted resources as success. If a trial hits the cap, preserve its charged failure and reassess feasibility; do not silently skip the planned controls and claim causation.
